header: Problem 7 Low-Valent Compounds of the Aluminum-Group Metals. Group 13 metals, the aluminum group (Al, Ga, In, Tl), can form chain, ring, and cluster compounds characterized by covalent metal-metal bonds and oxidation states below +III. Beginning with $E_2R_4$ compounds, this problem examines their bonding, stability, and reactivity. Chain and ring compounds have an E-E σ single bond (2c-2e) as their framework. After forming three covalent bonds, a metal has 6 valence-shell electrons and is Lewis acidic; the most common form is the $E_2R_4$ unit.

subquestions.text_open: 7.1 Based on the electronic properties of the $E_2R_4$ unit, which of the following can stabilize the $E_2R_4$ unit? A: R is a strongly electron-withdrawing group. B: R is a sterically bulky group. C: ligand L is added to form $R_2(L)E{-}E(L)R_2$.

7.2 "Dihalides" $E_2X_4$. Among the aluminum-group metals, Ga most readily forms $E_2X_4$, commonly as adduct $X_2(L)E{-}E(L)X_2$. If ligand L is also a halide anion, monoanionic or dianionic complexes form. 7.2.1 In one synthesis, Ga and $I_2$ react in toluene in a 2:1 molar ratio. After cooling to -78°C, 4 eq $NCy_2H$ is added. The mixture reacts for 12 h at room temperature, precipitate is removed by filtration, and the solution is concentrated and cooled to give colorless crystal A in 95% yield. Write the equations for the two steps forming A.

7.2.2 Replacing the ligand with the bulky N-heterocyclic carbene IPr and changing the feed ratio to n(Ga) : n($I_2$) : n(IPr) = 2 : 1 : 2 gives ionic compound B. The Ga mass fraction in B is 8.98%, and the principal MS FAB fragment peaks are m/z 389 (100%, $[IPrH]^+$) and 909 (61%, $[Ga_2I_3(IPr)]^+$). Write the SMILES structure of B.

subquestions.text_open: 7.2.3 Passing $NH_3$ into a THF solution of GaBr gives a precipitate. Extraction with DMF and crystallization give crystal C, $C_48H_112Br_18Ga_8N_16O_16$. C is an ionic compound with an anion:cation ratio of 3 : 2, and its anion contains a $Ga_2$ core. Write a chemical formula representing the structure of C.

7.3 $E_2R_4$, where R is alkyl or amino. $E_2R_4$ compounds are usually prepared by reaction of dihalide $E_2X_4L_2$ or subhalide EX with alkyl or amino anions. 7.3.1 Monodentate ligand, silyl: $Ga^{I}[Ga^{III}Cl_4]$ reacts with $Li(THF)_3Si(SiMe_3)_3$ to give D, E, or F depending on feed ratio. n($Ga^{I}[Ga^{III}Cl_4]$) : n($Li(THF)_3Si(SiMe_3)_3$) | product | MS (m/z) | Ga oxidation state | Ga coordination number | Ga chemical environment | Cl element | ideal symmetry. 1 : 1 | tetranuclear D | 1053 (4), 667 (11), 316 (80), 73 (100) | +2 | 4 | only one environment | contains Cl and all Cl environments are identical | $D_{2d}$. 1 : 2 | dinuclear E | 563 (10), 73 (100) | +2 | 3 | | no Cl | $D_{2d}$. 1 : 3 | tetranuclear F | | +1 | 4 | | no Cl | $T_{d}$. Write the SMILES structures of D, E, and F.

7.3.2 Bidentate ligand: the following dpp-bian ligand can coordinate as a monoanion or dianion. Its tripotassium salt $K_3[dpp-bian]$ reacts 1 : 1 with $GaCl_3$ in a reduction-coordination process to give dinuclear H_1. Its zinc salt $[(dpp-bian)ZnI]_2$ reacts with $GaCl_3$ and $K_4[dpp-bian]$ to give dinuclear H_2. Write SMILES structures reflecting their electronic properties, and explain why H_2 absorbs in the near-infrared at 950 nm whereas H_1 does not.

text_images.description: At far left, the figure shows ligand '[Ar]/N=C(/C2=N/[Ar])C3=CC=CC4=C3C2=CC=C4', labeled "dpp-bian", where Ar is 'CC(C)C1=CC=CC(C(C)C)=C1*', and two reaction pathways. In the upper path, `dpp-bian` reacts with `K (ex.)` in `THF` to form $K_4[dpp-bian]$, then with `+0.33 eq dpp-bian` to form $K_3[dpp-bian]$, and then under +$GaCl_3$ and `-3 KCl` gives H1, `[(dpp-bian)Ga-Ga(dpp-bian)]`. In the lower path, `dpp-bian` reacts with Zn (ex.), $I_2$ (0.5 eq), THF to form $[(dpp-bian)ZnI]_2$, then successively with $GaCl_3$ (2 eq) and $K_4[dpp-bian]$ (2 eq) to form H_2, `[(dpp-bian)Zn-Ga(dpp-bian)]`.

subquestions.text_open: 7.3.3 Tridentate ligand: in a suitable tridentate cage-ligand environment, the sixth-period element thallium (Tl) can rarely form a Tl-Tl metal bond. Tridentate ligand $H_3J$ = $(t{-}BuHN)_3SiMe$ can chelate one metal ion between every pair of nitrogen atoms and therefore bridge up to three metal atoms, forming diverse ring or cage structures. Reaction of $H_3J$ with excess n-BuLi in toluene gives dimeric lithium compound $(Li_3J)_2$, in which all Li atoms have identical environments and are three-coordinate to N. Reaction of $(Li_3J)_2$ with excess TlCl in dioxane gives dimeric thallium cluster $(Tl_3J)_2$, in which each Tl is two-coordinate to N and the cluster contains one relatively strong Tl-Tl bond. Write the SMILES structures of $(Li_3J)_2$ and $(Tl_3J)_2$.
